newsitem.title: UK: Brown's BOE move part of plan to ditch stg - Redwood.
newsitem.headline: Brown's BOE move part of plan to ditch stg - Redwood.

text.p: A candidate for the leadership of the opposition Conservative party on Tuesday accused Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown of following a plan to abolish the pound sterling.

John Redwood, regarded as the most right-wing Eurosceptical of the six contestants for John Major's job, claimed this was why Brown had opted to give the Bank of England operational control over key British interest rates.
Redwood was speaking at a press conference on the eve of the Queen's Speech setting out the government's legislative programme, which will include a bill to give the central bank additional powers.

"He (Brown) is slavishly following the tenets of the (European Union's) Maastricht Treaty," Redwood said. "The bill he is proposing is part of the plan to abolish the pound whatever the state of the western European economies."

Kenneth Clarke, who was Chancellor until the election, and who is the most left-wing of the leadership hopefuls, said on Monday that if the Conservatives lurched to the right in the leadership election, they could become unelectable.
But Redwood insisted that if he won the contest, he would be able to unite the party despite the presence in it of people like Clarke who are willing to contemplate joining the EU single currency.
"While I will not persuade Ken on the issue of principle for all time, I think I can persuade Ken that Labour's proposals will not be right," he said.

"Ken in the past has said a fudged single currency will be very damaging. I think we will only face a fudged single currency, so I think Ken and I can vote in the same lobby," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
